page.layout: One printed page (left page of the opening) with a main text column in the centre-right; a narrow margin of notes to the right edge of the scan belongs to the facing page and is not transcribed. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Heading CAPUT XXVI centred, with a sub-title, then the body text. Catchword "Status" at the foot right.

p.i: etiam erga alios peregrinos, cogitans se quoq; esse peregrinum, atque adeo non sit curiosus in aliena republica, nihil praeter negocium suum agat, nihil de alieno inquirat, moribus ac consuetudinibus istius loci in quo viuit, si non penitus sint absurda, sese accommodet.

main_text.p: Postrema pars Canonis, nempe quod peregrinus no debeat esse curiosus in aliena rep. sunt verba Cic. 1. de rep. videri autem potest de hac materia latius c.4. lib.4. Tolosd. de rep.
main_text.head: CAPVT XXVI. De causis primis mutationum in republ.

p.i: Hvcusq; de statu reipub. integro & incorrupto: Sequitur status reipu. affectus & morbosus.

main_text.p: Cum hactenus egerimus de perfecti status Politici, nempe de Monarchiae, siue principatus fundamentis siue causis, postea etiam effectis, siue officio tum respectu principis, tum subditorum; iam nunc methodi ratio nos ducit ad opposita, siue pugnantia status perfecti. Pugnat autem cum statu perfecto status affectus, siue mutatio, inclinatio & euersio status Politici, de quo in disciplina Politica necessario tractandum est, vt nempe remedia quaeri possint pro mutatione & euersione status vel auertenda, vel curanda & emendanda; quandoquidem haec est proprietas statuum Pol. in hac conditione humani generis, vt multis mutationib. corruptionib. & veluti morbis magis vel minus lethalibus sint obnoxii.

page.notes: Partly damaged at the left edge and in the lower left. The word "Pol" at the far right and the small marginal words belong to the facing page and were not transcribed. Uncertain readings: "Cum" (initial C partly obscured) and the word after "effectis" are printed as seen.
